title: Definition
body_md: Given a positive integer $s$, a subset of vertices $S\subseteq V$ is an $s$-plex if every vertex in $S$ is adjacent to at least $|S|-s$ other vertices of $S$. Equivalently, every vertex in $S$ has at most $s-1$ non-neighbors in $S$.

body_md: Given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ and a non-negative integer vector $b\in \mathbb{Z}_n^+$, a subset of edges $M\subseteq E$ is said to be a $b$-matching in $G$ if no vertex $i\in V$ is incident to more than $b_i$ edges in $M$.

name: First-order stationary point

label: prop_convergence_y
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, we show that the function $y\rightarrow h_G(x,y)$ is strongly convex on $[0,1]^{\bar{m}}\supset P'_s(G)$ with a convexity coefficient $\mu = 2\beta(\gamma - 1)>0$, since $\gamma>1$. Since this function is separable with respect to $y$, in the one-dimensional case we can consider $f(t):=w(x)t + \beta t(t-1)(t+\gamma) + c(x)$, $\forall t\in[0,1]$,  for fixed $x$. Although $w(x)$ and $c(x)$ may depend on $x$, they are respectively a coefficient of a linear term and a constant term with respect to $t$; therefore they do not contribute to the second derivative. Indeed, we get $f''(t)=2\beta(3t + \gamma-1)\geq2\beta(\gamma-1)$, since $f''$ reaches its minimum in $[0,1]$ for $t=0$. This shows that $f$ is strongly convex in $[0,1]$ with the strong-convexity coefficient $\mu:=2\beta(\gamma-1)$. Because the Hessian with respect to $y$ of $h_G(x,y)$ is diagonal with entries $f''(y_{ij})$, the same bound applies in $\bar{m}$ dimensions. 
    
    Now assume that $y^{(k)}$ and $y^{(k+1)}$ are two distinct vertices of $P'_s(G)$. Let $z^{(k)}=(x^{(k+1)}, y^{(k)})$ and $z^{(k+1)}=(x^{(k+1)}, y^{(k+1)})$. By the strong convexity just established  for $y\rightarrow h_G(x,y)$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        h_G(z^{(k+1)}) - h_G(z^{(k)})&\geq\nabla h_G(z^{(k)})^\top (z^{(k+1)}-z^{(k)}) + \frac{\mu}{2}\|z^{(k+1)} - z^{(k)}\|^2 \\
        &= \nabla_yh_G(z^{(k)})^\top (y^{(k+1)} - y^{(k)}) + \frac{\mu}{2}\|y^{(k+1)} - y^{(k)}\|^2 \\
        &\geq \frac{\mu}{2}\|y^{(k+1)} - y^{(k)}\|^2\geq \frac{\mu}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\mu}{4}. 
    \end{align*}
    The first-order term is non-negative because $y^{(k+1)}$ is an
optimal solution of the linear problem in step~\ref{step:FWa2} of Algorithm \ref{ FW$s$P} and $y^{(k)}$ is feasible. Moreover, the squared distance between two distinct vertices of $P'_s(G)$ is at least $1/2$. Indeed, the vertices are
half-integral, and a single difference of size $1/2$ would contradict the odd-cycle characterization of their fractional support.
                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                
The previous inequality accounts only for the $y$ update. To obtain an increase between two consecutive iterates, we use the assumption  on the $x$ update. As a consequence, whenever  $y^{(k+1)}\neq y^{(k)}$, we have $h_G(x^{(k+1)},y^{(k+1)})
-h_G(x^{(k)},y^{(k)})
\geq \frac{\mu}{4}.$  Hence, these increases can be telescoped over all iterations in which
the $y$-component changes.
    Therefore, $y^{(k)}$ can change at most 
    \begin{align*}
        \max_{(x,y)\in\Delta_n\times P'_s(G)} &\frac{h_G(x,y)-h_G(x^{(0)},y^{(0)})}{\frac{\mu}{4}} \\
        &\leq\frac{4}{\mu}\Big(\max_{(x,y)\in\Delta_n\times P'_s(G)}h_G(x,y)\ \ - \min_{(x,y)\in\Delta_n\times P'_s(G)}h_G(x,y)\Big) \\
        &\leq \frac{4}{\mu}\Big(1-\frac{2-\alpha}{2|C^*|} - \frac{\alpha}{2n} + \frac{\beta\bar{m}}{4}(\gamma + 1)\Big) \\
        &= \frac{2}{\beta(\gamma-1)}\Big(1-\frac{2-\alpha}{2|C^*|} - \frac{\alpha}{2n} + \frac{\beta\bar{m}}{4}(\gamma + 1)\Big)
    \end{align*}
    times, where we used Corollary \ref{corollary_global_equivalence} with an $s$-plex $C^*$ of maximum cardinality in $G$, and the fact that
    \begin{align*}
        \min_{(x,y)\in\Delta_n\times P'_s(G)}h_G(x,y) &\geq \frac{\alpha}{2n} + \min_{y\in P'_s(G)}\beta\sum_{\{i,j\}\in\bar{E}}y_{ij}(y_{ij}-1)(y_{ij}+\gamma)\\
        &\geq\frac{\alpha}{2n} + \beta\bar{m}\min_{t\in[0,1]}t(t-1)(t+\gamma)\\
        &=\frac{\alpha}{2n} -\beta\bar{m}\max_{t\in[0,1]}t(1-t)(t+\gamma)\\
        &\geq\frac{\alpha}{2n} -\beta\bar{m}\max_{t\in[0,1]}t(1-t)\cdot\max_{t\in[0,1]}(t+\gamma)\\
        &=\frac{\alpha}{2n} -\frac{\beta\bar{m}}{4}(\gamma + 1).
    \end{align*}
This is obtained by considering that the adjacency contribution to $h_G$ is non-negative and $||x||_2^2\geq1/n$ for every $x\in\Delta_n$. 
Finally, if after this number of iterations the $y$-component of the solution corresponds to a fractional vertex of $P'_s(G)$, then the algorithm simply sets all fractional components to zero in the subsequent iteration. This occurs because the weights given by the gradient and associated with the fractional components of the solution are strictly negative in this case, since $\beta>2$.

title: Remark
body_md:
For $\beta>0$ and $\gamma>1$, the strong-convexity argument still
implies finite stabilization of the $y$-sequence, using only the
boundedness of the objective on the compact feasible set. The stronger
condition $\beta>2$ is needed to ensure that the stabilized vertex is
binary and to invoke the equivalence results of Section~\ref{section_3}.
We also observe that the monotonicity assumption in Proposition~\ref{prop_convergence_y} is satisfied under the hypotheses of the convergence result below. Indeed, condition~\eqref{cond2_stepsize}, together with the fact that the direction selected by the AFW method is an ascent direction, implies
$
h_G(x^{(k+1)},y^{(k)})
\geq h_G(x^{(k)},y^{(k)}).
$
Consequently, Proposition~\ref{prop_convergence_y} applies under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{th_convergence}.

label: th_convergence
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop_convergence_y}, after finitely many iterations, the $y$-variable generated by Algorithm~\ref{ FW$s$P} stabilizes at a binary vertex $y^*\in P'_s(G)$. Thereafter, the algorithm reduces to the AFW method applied over the standard simplex to maximize the quadratic function
$
h_G(x,y^*)=x^\top A_{G^*}x+\frac{\alpha}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2.
$ As already noticed, the considered optimization problem corresponds to a regularized version of the MS for the MCP over the auxiliary graph $G^*$ induced by the binary vector $y^*$. 
    
   For $\alpha=1$, the fixed-$y$ objective can be written as $h_G(x,y^*)
=
x^\top Q_{G^*}x,$ with 
$Q_{G^*}:=A_{G^*}+\frac{1}{2}\mathbb I_n.
$
                                                                                                                                                         
                
                                      
              
                                                                                                                                                                                    
                
                                        
              
                                        
By the argument used in the proof of Theorem~$12$ in \cite{bomze1999genetic}, every principal submatrix of $Q_{G^*}$ is nonsingular. Consequently, by Theorem~$8$ therein, there can be at most one stationary point in the relative interior of each face of the standard simplex when $y^*$ is fixed. Furthermore, Theorem~$2.5$ in \cite{massaro2002complementary} implies that there exist finitely many stationary points of the fixed-$y$ problem, all satisfying strict complementarity and having distinct supports. Therefore, all the assumptions of Theorem~$4.5$ in \cite{AFW} are satisfied, and the sequence $\{x^{(k)}\}_k$ converges to a stationary point $x^*$ of the fixed-$y$ problem and identifies its support in finite time.

It remains to verify stationarity with respect to the $y$-component. Since $y^{(k+1)}=y^{(k)}=y^*$ for every sufficiently large $k$, step~\ref{step:FWa2} of Algorithm~\ref{ FW$s$P} gives
\begin{align*}
    \nabla_y h_G(x^{(k+1)},y^*)^\top(\bar y-y^*)\leq0
    \qquad\text{for every }\bar y\in P'_s(G).
\end{align*}
Passing to the limit, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \nabla_y h_G(x^*,y^*)^\top(\bar y-y^*)\leq0
    \qquad\text{for every }\bar y\in P'_s(G).
\end{align*}
Combining this inequality with the stationarity of $x^*$ for the fixed-$y$ problem shows that
$\nabla h_G(x^*,y^*)^\top
    \big((\bar x,\bar y)-(x^*,y^*)\big)\leq0 $
for every $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\Delta_n\times P'_s(G)$. Hence, $(x^*,y^*)$ is a first-order stationary point in the sense of Definition~\ref{def_stationary_point}. Finally, since $y^{(k)}$ becomes constant and the AFW method identifies $\operatorname{supp}(x^*)$ in finite time, the complete sequence converges to $(x^*,y^*)$ and identifies the support of its $x$-component in finite time.
